LAW AND MOTION 301, NO APPEARANCES ON THIS MATTER DESPITE A HEARING WAS REQUIRED BY THE COURT. THE COURT WAS DISTURBED BY THE FACT THAT NOBODY APPEARED ON EITHER SIDE. AS INDICATED IN THE COURT'S TENTATIVE RULING, PLAINTIFF APPEARS TO HAVE TRIED TO INVOKE A TIMELY CHALLENGE TO JUDGE BUSCH PURSUANT TO CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE SECTION 170.6, BUT HIS DECLARATION FILED ON FEB. 19 DOES NOT INCLUDE ALL THE STATEMENTS REQUIRED BY SECTION 170.6(A)(5). THE COURT THEREFORE STRIKE THAT TO THE EXTENT IT WAS INDEED A 170.6 CHALLENGE. IF IT WAS A CHALLENGE PURSUANT TO 170.1 AND 170.3, IT WAS NOT IN PROPER FORM AND NOT PROPERLY SERVED. THE CASE IS THEREFORE BEFORE THE COURT. DEFENDANT CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF CORRECTIONS AND REHABILITATION'S DEMURRER TO COMPLAINT AND MOTION TO DISMISS- THE COURT SUSTAINED THE DEMURRER WITH 10 DAYS LEAVE TO AMEND IF THE PLAINTIFF CAN IN GOOD FAITH PROVE COMPLIANCE WITH THE TORT CLAIM ACT REQUIREMENTS FOR SUBMISSION OF A CLAIM. MOVING PARTY TO PREPARE FORM OF ORDER. THE COURT WENT BACK ON THE RECORD FOR THE SECOND TIME TO INDICATE A CORRECTION TO THE RULING. IF PLAINTIFF CHOOSES TO FILE AN AMENDED DECLARATION PRIOR TO THE HEARING WHICH THE COURT HAS NOT RECEIVED AND WILL BE CHECKING IF INDEED THERE IS ONE, THE COURT WILL STEP DOWN AND VACATE THE SUBSTANTIVE RULING.
